to this. Marty, you've had a fascinating career. Obviously, you played a really pivotal role in turning the

ways. And some scientists had this idea crazy at the time that we could simulate

first job was working on these big Fortran programs that would use Monte Carlo

individual competent electrons being scattered out of a neutron bomb explosion and then calculate the electro

the tourism business. And so I did that. And then the next bit. And then the next
big moment was I went to Harvard, I was a kid, and I took sophomore standing.

declare. It was going to be some kind of science, for sure. And I went to the
Science Center and the science professors were recruiting for their departments.

building digital twins of biology that it seemed obvious to me, that it seemed obvious to me that

And this is a big problem. And we made some inroads, but it was clear that the computers were

to make a list of entrepreneurs in Silicon Valley with PhDs and computer science from Stanford. And

It was a little less than perfect.
